children: U.S. soybean futures rose on Thursday, as traders assessed progress in Chinese purchases of U.S. supplies and looked ahead to a meeting between presidents Donald Trump and Xi Jinping.
on the Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) was up 0.74% at $13.30-1/4 a bushel, as of 0504 GMT, hovering near its highest level in almost three years.
China has now passed the halfway mark toward its commitment to buy 25 million metric tons of U.S. soybeans, agreed during the Busan summit last October.
U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Tuesday that he planned to meet his Chinese counterpart He Lifeng this weekend, ahead of the leaders' meeting next week.
Rain in parts of the upper Midwest has delayed harvesting, lending some support to soybean and corn prices, according to two Chinese analysts.
added 0.27% to $7.32-3/4 a bushel, supported in part by expectations of a smaller Canadian crop.
Canadian farmers will produce 11% less wheat and about the same amount of canola as they did last year, Statistics Canada said on Wednesday in its first crop production report of 2026.
Jordan's state grain buyer has issued an international tender to buy up to 120,000 metric tons of milling wheat that can be sourced from optional origins, European traders said.

Traders continued to assess risks to grain exports from the Black Sea region. Russian air strikes damaged buildings in Kyiv and injured three people in the Black Sea port city of Odesa early on Thursday, Ukrainian officials said.
Commodity funds were net sellers of CBOT corn and soybean futures, traders said on Wednesday. (CBOT/FUNDS)
